messages:
Maria: heads up — since the allocator tweak landed last night we've seen two OOMs on p3-heavy long-chat workloads. logs look like fragmentation, not total memory pressure.
Kevin: which tweak exactly? the small-chunk fallback or the workspace reuse patch?
Maria: workspace reuse patch (PR #4821) + aggressive shrink-to-fit after eviction. stacktrace: `cudaMalloc: out of memory` but free pool had ~1.8GB fragmented in many 64–256KB blocks.
Sanjay: oof. that matches what the profiler showed yesterday: large number of small free blocks, free-list churn spikes during prefixcache TTL eviction sweeps.
Eva: can you paste the perf counters? I want to see allocation sizes distribution.
Maria: pasted below — short sample during an eviction cycle (50s window):
```
alloc_count_total: 12.3k
avg_alloc_size: 48.6KB
median_alloc_size: 18KB
max_alloc_size: 3.1MB
free_segments: 4121
largest_free_segment: 2.1MB
gpu_used: 9.2GB / 16GB
prefixcache_mem: 2.8GB
kv_shard_active: 6 shards
```
Kevin: two quick notes: (1) kernel selection for large-attn paths sometimes asks for extra workspace allocations per layer (cuBLAS/cuDNN), (2) continuous batching causes transient peak allocations when many short requests hit simultaneously.
Jamie: the interesting bit is TTL sweep evictions are causing repeated small allocations because we immediately allocate small temp buffers per-eviction-job. If eviction threads run in parallel we fragment the pool.
Maria: agreed. our sim showed that with TTL=60s and 8 shards we had ~12% higher fragmentation score vs TTL=300s.
Sanjay: do we have hit-rate vs TTL numbers? would like to quantify impact on tail latency and cost.
Maria: quick table from the simulation harness (same workload; 24h trace):
```
TTL  | cache_mem | hit_rate | avg_lat_ms | fragmentation_score
30s | 3.1GB     | 0.64     | 78ms       | 0.47
60s | 2.9GB     | 0.68     | 72ms       | 0.39
300s| 2.6GB     | 0.74     | 63ms       | 0.21
```
Eva: interesting — shorter TTL increases mem footprint and fragmentation. Looks like churn -> alloc/free delta.
Kevin: mitigation shortlist: 1) switch to a slab allocator for small sizes, 2) pool eviction workspaces per-shard instead of allocating on the fly, 3) change batching heuristics to smooth concurrent evictions, 4) increase TTL for shards with high churn.
Maria: I prototyped (2) — per-shard preallocated workspace pool (config below). It eliminated ~85% of small allocs during eviction windows in local test.
```
{"prefixcache": {"shards": 8, "eviction_workspace_per_shard": "8MB", "eviction_worker_threads": 2}}
```
Jamie: nice. any downside? more reserved memory on idle.
Maria: yes tradeoff: we reserve ~64MB across 8 shards (8MB*8) which is small vs 16GB, but for many small GPUs or constrained Dedicated boxes it's non-zero. Also needs accounting in the allocator so reserved chunks don't get counted as available for kernels.
Sanjay: alternative is to make the workspace pooled but lazily backed by a single large buffer that can be sub-allocated; reduces fragmentation but not increase idle reservation.
Kevin: also consider changing kernel selection thresholds: prefer kernels that don't request huge ephemeral workspace when many small requests present. We have telemetry that cuDNN fused kernels request extra scratch for longer seq-len thresholds. Lowering threshold helps at small sequence distributions.
Maria: I ran a quick kernel selection experiment: clipping kernel to favor lower-workspace variant for sequence <=64 reduced peak allocs by 18% and had 1.5% throughput regression on long sequences.

Eva: that's promising — small perf hit but better stability. For Dedicated customers we could expose this knob per-deployment.
Jamie: regarding shard sizing: maybe autoscale shard count based on active prefix cardinality. fewer shards -> fewer concurrent eviction threads -> less fragmentation, but increases per-shard memory and reduces parallelism.
Sanjay: right. we simulated dynamic shard count: when active prefixes < N we collapse to M shards, and expand when above. It reduced fragmentation spikes by ~22% in trace. Need safe thresholds.
Maria: action items we agreed on:
- short-term: roll back shrink-to-fit aggressive path and enable per-shard eviction workspace pool (config toggle), and clip kernel selection threshold for seq<=64. (Owner: Maria)
- medium: prototype lazy suballocator for eviction workspaces and slab allocator for small sizes (Owner: Sanjay)
- medium: add telemetry: fragmentation_score, free_segment_histogram, per-shard eviction_alloc_count to console dashboards. (Owner: Eva)
- longer: shard autoscaling POC integrated into router to avoid noisy parallel eviction. (Owner: Kevin)

Maria: I'll open PRs for the rollback and the workspace-pool today and include a small sim with the 24h trace.
ops-bot: deploy bot: patch-rollback-ci ran and found one failing test (memory-accounting-test). CI link: https://ci.redwood/patches/4821/rollback-checks
Kevin: I'll look at the failing test, might be expected due to reserved workspace accounting.
Jamie: thanks all — schedule a quick sync if we see another OOM in the next 24h. :thumbsup:
